discrepancies.title: OM claims 17.0% rental uplift; the screen reference supports at most 4.4% at renewal or on re-letting to the screen reference

sources.quote: As leases renew and re-let through 2027, we expect gross income to rise by c.AED 1.90m (+17%) within 12 months.
sources.label: OM upside claim
largest renewal increase any tenant can get in the next 24 months (RERA bands, notice period)
largest uplift including re-letting to the screen reference on turnover

discrepancies.why: At renewal a tenant's rent can rise only within the RERA band for how far its own rent sits below the index (the top band allows 20%), with prior written notice; on turnover a unit re-lets at market, uncapped. Applied unit by unit against the screen reference, the claim of 17.0% is beyond the 4.4% the reference supports at renewal or on re-letting to the screen reference. The screen reference is a proxy for the RERA index: confirm unit by unit with the DLD Smart Rental Index calculator.

impact.basis: uplift the screen reference supports minus the OM claim

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ignore the claimed reversion; ask the broker which units it relies on and check each in the DLD Smart Rental Index calculator.

discrepancies.title: Operating statement covers 9 months but is presented as a full year
discrepancies.why: Annualising part of a year misstates seasonal and one-off costs (insurance renewals, annual maintenance contracts) and hides recent changes. amounts are already annualised by the seller from 9 months.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Request a full year of monthly statements, with the general ledger for one-off items.

notices.text: Tenants' security deposits of AED 540,100 transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
Cheque profile: 43% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 32% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 25% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Building condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age (MEP, lifts, facade, waterproofing).

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: at asking price the deal misses the mandate's going-in yield, unlevered IRR and equity multiple targets, so it only works at a much lower price.

Buy at AED 79.5m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], exit at 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]]. That is 37% below asking [[uw.walk_away_vs_asking]], against an ask of AED 125.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. The assumption that most moves the walk-away price is the reference rent path, at 5% [[uw.walk_away_most_sensitive]] either way, which moves the price by AED 10.1m [[uw.walk_away_largest_swing_aed]]. The walk-away price and the returns rest on the firm's house view (reference rents, exit yield, vacancy and downtime), not on market evidence for this building.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Larkspur Residence, Arjan, Al Barsha South; 126 units [[om.unit_count]], completed 2016 [[deal.completion_year]]. The mix is 70 1BR [[rr.1br.units]], 42 2BR [[rr.2br.units]] and 14 studios [[rr.studio.units]].
- **Price:** AED 125.5m [[uw.price_aed]], or AED 1,012 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA. Total cost with acquisition costs is AED 133.3m [[uw.total_cost_aed]].
- **Income:** in-place rent is AED 11.2m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] at 95% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy. 120 units [[rr.let_units]] are let and 6 [[rr.vacant_units]] are vacant. Leases are direct, with no master tenant. The largest expiry block is 31% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of rent (AED 3.4m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]]), between 30 April 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 30 July 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]].

## Returns
Unlevered, pre-tax:

| Metric | Screen | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR | 2.1% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] | 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] |
| Equity multiple | 1.10x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 5.7% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |
| Entry yield on price | 6.0% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |

Year-1 NOI is AED 7.6m [[uw.noi_year1]]. Exit value is AED 110.9m [[uw.gross_exit_value_aed]], below the purchase price.

Levered, secondary: a loss of 0.8% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] a year, equity multiple 0.96x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]], Year-1 DSCR 1.40x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM headline yield is 6.0% [[om.yield_stated]], net on total cost. On the buyer's basis it is 5.7% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]], which is 0.3 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]] lower.

## What would make it fail
- **Rents:** the house view has market rents falling 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower, unlevered IRR is 0.5% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]]. Adding an exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider turns that into a loss of 0.6% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]].
- **No upside case reaches target:** with market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter, unlevered IRR is 4.8% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]], still under 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]].
- **Expiry bunching:** 31% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of rent expires in one three-month window, so re-letting terms matter in 2027.
- **Unverified reference rent:** the screen's reference rent for this area is marked unverified, and the rent path and walk-away price depend on it.

## Discrepancies
**Uplift claim (high).** The OM expects gross income to rise c.AED 1.90m [[om.upside_claim_1]], about 17% [[om.upside_claim_1]], within 12 months as leases renew. The screen relied on its reference rent, applied unit by unit. That supports at most 4.4% [[disc.upside_exceeds_rera_cap.why]] at renewal or on re-letting, and renewal increases are limited by RERA rent-increase bands. The claim runs 13 points [[disc.upside_exceeds_rera_cap.impact_ratio]] beyond what the reference supports. We gave it no credit. The reference is a proxy for the RERA index, so it needs unit-by-unit confirmation.

**Part-year statement (medium).** The operating statement covers 9 months [[opex.months]], and the seller annualised it. That can misstate seasonal and one-off costs and hide recent changes. The screen used the statement but rebuilt income and costs. Its Year-1 NOI is AED 7.6m [[bridge.screen_noi_year1_aed]] against AED 7.8m [[bridge.statement_noi_aed]] on the statement.

Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Checks before diligence
- Ask the broker which units the uplift claim relies on. Check each in the DLD Smart Rental Index calculator.
- Get a full year of monthly statements, with the general ledger for one-off items.
- Verify the screen reference rent for Al Barsha South.
- Security deposits of AED 540,100 [[notice.security_deposits]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Cheque profile: 25% [[notice.cheque_profile]] of rent is on six or more cheques, which means more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold, single title, buyer eligibility.
- Dubai Municipality completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll.
- Civil Defence certificates and ACP cladding compliance.
- Building condition survey and capex plan.

## Assumptions
The exit yield of 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]] is the higher of the area and entry yields, plus 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion and an age premium. Market rents fall 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and 1% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2. They then rise 2% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]], collection loss 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]], renewal probability 70% [[assume.renewal_probability]] and the hold is 5 years [[uw.hold_years]]. Debt is 40% [[uw.ltv]] loan to value at 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]], sized at a 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] DSCR, with amortisation over 15 years [[assume.amortisation_years]]. No operating cost categories were filled from mandate defaults.
